answers.U1-S1: A six-year-old boy walks two miles with his brothers to a river on the pampas and sees lots of wild birds, like ducks, swans, herons and flamingos.
answers.U1-S2: He was terrified of them, so his brother had to promise there was no herd and he would stay away from anything with horns.
answers.U1-S3: To show they had to take many turns to avoid them, and the grass was full of flowers like an English meadow in June.
answers.U1-S4: In a row, evenly spaced a yard or so apart from each other.
answers.U1-S5: Because when the wings were open they were a glorious crimson colour.
answers.U1-S6: That flamingos weren't known in their neighbourhood because the water-courses there weren't large enough, though they lived at a lake a day away.
answers.U1-S7: Because when it opened and shook its wings they were a glorious crimson colour.
answers.U1-S8: He saw them hundreds of times, at sunset, in the early morning and flying in flocks, but it never equalled when he was six.
answers.U1-S9: It describes all the later times he saw flamingos, standing in still water or flying low over the water in a long crimson line.
answers.U1-S10: He still feels delight about it; nothing he saw later ever equalled that first time.
